next_three_research_scopes.title: Chunk-size choices for causal long prefill under GPU memory limits
next_three_research_scopes.finite_question: For long causal or recurrent GPU prefill, compare smaller, current-size and larger chunks, including short-tail handling. Which workload and device conditions justify each choice when matrix-tile utilization, launch amortization, live workspace, memory traffic and shared-state dependencies all matter?
next_three_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use current SYCL/Intel primary documentation and original non-LLM GPU or accelerator papers and engineering reports. Compare at least three chunk-size strategies plus a tail strategy. Include cases where smaller chunks save workspace but lose to launch overhead or tile underfill, and where larger chunks improve amortization but worsen residency, tail waste or memory pressure. Distinguish published measurements from design estimates and report portability limits. Do not re-cover fixed-buffer queue/overlap scheduling, claim B570 performance, or propose a product change.
next_three_research_scopes.report_budget: 1300–1800 words; at most 7 substantive primary sources, exact links, an applicability table and explicit counterevidence.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisites: None beyond public-source access; this bounded knowledge collection does not require a new local measurement or the pending NLL result.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisite_evidence: AGENTS.md keeps long-prefill chunk-size tuning active. The indexed R769 report compares fixed 8192-row storage and queue schedules but does not compare chunk sizes. Any later implementation decision remains subject to Main's full-path measurement and physical-context correctness requirements.

next_three_research_scopes.title: Host CPU cost and latency tradeoffs in GPU completion waits
next_three_research_scopes.finite_question: Across SYCL, Unified Runtime and Level Zero workloads, compare active polling, blocking or low-power event waits, interrupt-backed notification, and adaptive spin-then-sleep approaches for repeated GPU completion waits. How do queue depth, wait duration, event setup, OS scheduling and device signaling affect host CPU use, completion latency and end-to-end throughput?
next_three_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use official SYCL/UR/Level Zero specifications and original non-LLM GPU/HPC measurements or engineering reports. Compare at least three completion strategies and distinguish API guarantees from measured implementation behavior. Include cases where sleeping reduces CPU consumption but increases wake latency or injects extra device signaling, and cases where active polling is appropriate for short waits. R751 already covers the current API semantics and a source-level diagnostic plan; do not restate it. Focus on independent empirical comparisons, across-runtime limits and evidence needed before selecting a policy. Do not assert that the supplied wait CPU time identifies a particular driver stack or that changing a wait policy improves Strata.
next_three_research_scopes.report_budget: 1200–1700 words; at most 7 substantive primary sources, exact links, a strategy comparison matrix and counterevidence.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisites: None beyond public-source access; the task is a literature comparison and does not require the pending NLL run or another local wait measurement.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisite_evidence: Main supplied a current attribution of 165.704 CPU seconds in explicit waits. R751 established only that busy polling is plausible for this runtime family and that source call timing cannot prove the internal stack; the new measurement makes broader empirical tradeoff evidence relevant without proving a cause or remedy.

next_three_research_scopes.title: Transfer granularity and packing for repeated host-to-GPU data movement
next_three_research_scopes.finite_question: For repeated GPU workloads that move segmented, strided or otherwise noncontiguous input data, compare issuing many small copies, packing data into a contiguous host staging region, batching transfers by compatible ranges, and gathering into GPU-local storage. Under what payload sizes, reuse patterns and compute budgets does each choice reduce total host work and dependency-path time?
next_three_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use official SYCL/Intel documentation plus original non-LLM GPU, database or scientific-computing studies and engineering reports. Compare at least three strategies with attention to host packing cost, copy-call/runtime overhead, link utilization, extra GPU gather work, registration behavior, buffer lifetime and ordering. Include counterexamples where packing costs more CPU than the transfer savings, direct copy is already efficient, or a GPU gather adds a launch and memory traffic. Distinguish logical bytes from measured link traffic. R762 compares mapped-host access with explicit copy; R765 examines a possible UR host-copy path; keep this investigation on granularity and packing crossovers, not those same mechanisms. Do not recommend blanket pinning or claim a Strata speedup.
next_three_research_scopes.report_budget: 1300–1800 words; at most 7 substantive primary sources, exact links, a workload crossover table and evidence limits.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisites: None beyond public-source access; current Main-supplied results are enough to motivate a knowledge collection and no follow-up experiment is required for the report.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisite_evidence: Main supplied a 25.793-second residual copy-call CPU cost that includes hidden runtime work, plus an idle 320 MiB Host USM transfer at 5.095 GB/s versus 6.015 GB/s for ordinary transfer. These figures motivate comparison but do not establish copy granularity as the bottleneck or explain the bandwidth difference.
